record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Given a morphism f and a letter a such that a is the initial letter of f(a), is it decidable whether the fixed point f^ω(a) is quasiperiodic?

evidence.quote: Given a morphism f and a letter a such that a is the initial letter of f (a), is it decidable that f^^ω(a) is quasiperiodic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet, and let A* (resp. A^ω) denote the set of finite (resp. one-sided infinite) words over A. A morphism f : A* → A* extends to A^ω by concatenation. A letter a ∈ A is called prolongable under f if f(a) starts with a and |f^n(a)| → ∞ as n → ∞; in this case the iterates f^n(a) converge to a unique infinite word f^ω(a) ∈ A^ω, called the pure morphic fixed point of f starting at a, satisfying f(f^ω(a)) = f^ω(a).

A finite nonempty word q ∈ A* is called a quasiperiod of an infinite word w ∈ A^ω if every position of w lies inside at least one occurrence of q in w (equivalently, w can be covered by occurrences of q). The infinite word w is called quasiperiodic if it admits at least one quasiperiod.

Problem. Determine whether the following decision problem is decidable:

  Input: a finite alphabet A, a morphism f : A* → A*, and a letter a ∈ A such that f(a) begins with a (so that the fixed point f^ω(a) is well-defined as an infinite word).
  Question: Is f^ω(a) quasiperiodic?

That is, does there exist an algorithm that, given any such (A, f, a), decides whether the pure morphic fixed point f^ω(a) admits a quasiperiod?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not turn up an explicit resolution of the decidability of quasiperiodicity for pure morphic fixed points. Related results are known: ultimate periodicity of morphic words is decidable (Harju–Linna; Pansiot), and there exist methods to compute the set of quasiperiods of certain morphic words, but no general decidability result for quasiperiodicity of arbitrary morphic fixed points was located. The problem appears to remain open, though this could not be confirmed conclusively.

status_evidence.title: On the Periodicity of Morphic Words
status_evidence.snippet: It is decidable whether a morphic word is ultimately p-periodic.
status_evidence.claim: Periodicity (not quasiperiodicity) of morphic words is known to be decidable.

status_evidence.title: Quasiperiods in infinite words (Oxford seminar)
status_evidence.snippet: Methods to determine the set of quasiperiods of an infinite word, especially morphic words.
status_evidence.claim: Quasiperiods can be computed in some cases for morphic words, but no general decidability theorem stated.

status_evidence.title: The Maximal Complexity of Quasiperiodic Infinite Words
status_evidence.snippet: Marcus posed several questions on quasiperiodic infinite words; subsequent work addresses complexity questions.
status_evidence.claim: Research on quasiperiodicity of infinite words is ongoing; no resolution of the decidability question for morphic fixed points was located.
